summary: Implementation cleanly exposes five new CRD fields (spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds, spec.preStopSleepSeconds, spec.strategy, spec.uwsgi.harakiri, spec.uwsgi.httpKeepAliveTimeout), wires them through the reconciler with pure nil-safe helpers (terminationGracePeriodSeconds, preStopSleepSeconds, deploymentStrategy), and enforces all cross-field invariants (preStop<grace, harakiri<grace-preStop, keepAliveTimeout requires httpKeepAlive, Recreate excludes rollingUpdate block) in the validating webhook with defense-in-depth alongside kubebuilder markers. Nil pointers resolve to defaults (30/5) before the drain-window arithmetic — verified by TestValidate_PreStopEqualsDefaultGraceRejected and TestValidate_HarakiriAtDrainBoundaryRejected. uwsgiCommand strictly gates both new optional flags on non-nil pointers so no empty --flag '' is ever emitted; --http-keepalive-timeout is additionally gated on httpKeepAlive=true. buildKeystoneDeployment always writes Spec.Strategy via a value-returning helper (no zero-value code path). The helm/ and config/crd/bases/ CRD bodies are byte-identical (modulo the three-line CC-0017 header). Unit, envtest, and chainsaw E2E coverage is comprehensive and test naming exactly matches the REQ scenarios. Documentation (architecture HA doc + keystone-crd reference) is thorough and consistently carries CC-0084 identifiers. No blocking issues found; a handful of small tightening opportunities are offered as suggestions.

tests_checklist.notes: keystone_types_test.go adds TestKeystoneSpecTerminationGracePeriodSecondsField, TestKeystoneSpecStrategyField, extended TestUWSGISpecFields for Harakiri/HTTPKeepAliveTimeout. keystone_webhook_test.go covers all CC-0084 webhook rules including the critical nil-resolves-to-default case (TestValidate_PreStopEqualsDefaultGraceRejected) and the drain-window boundary (TestValidate_HarakiriAtDrainBoundaryRejected, TestValidate_HarakiriAboveDrainRejected, TestValidate_HarakiriWithinDrainAccepted). reconcile_deployment_test.go exercises flag emission with indexOf helpers (not brittle full-array equality), FlagOrderDeterministic, StrategyDefaultedAndStable, TerminationGracePeriodDefault/Custom, PreStopSleepDefault/Custom/Zero, StrategyOverrideRollingCustomPercents, StrategyOverrideRecreate. integration_test.go adds three envtest cases that apply a real CR and assert the pod template. Chainsaw e2e test tests/e2e/keystone/rolling-update-zero-downtime/ asserts zero 5xx AND availableReplicas>=3 with >=200 requests and >=30 samples, with rich catch/diagnostic scripts.

code_quality_checklist.notes: Helper functions terminationGracePeriodSeconds(), preStopSleepSeconds(), deploymentStrategy() mirror the existing priorityClassName()/containerResources() pattern in reconcile_deployment.go. Comments on new helpers correctly document the CC-0084 rationale (why 30s default, why always emit the hook block, why a fresh value per call). uwsgiCommand has a comment block explaining append order and why --harakiri precedes --http-keepalive-timeout. go vet ./operators/keystone/... passes cleanly in the worktree. All new code and tests reference CC-0084 per the Feature-ID rule.

security_checklist.notes: Defense-in-depth bounds validation on all four new Minimum-marked fields in the webhook (terminationGracePeriodSeconds>=10, preStopSleepSeconds>=0, harakiri>=1, httpKeepAliveTimeout>=1) plus cross-field rules protects the operator from CRs submitted via reduced-schema paths. Load generator Job runs non-root uid 100, allowPrivilegeEscalation:false, seccompProfile:RuntimeDefault, drops ALL capabilities, automountServiceAccountToken:false. Load-gen stays inside the cluster via keystone-rolling-update-api.openstack.svc and hits the Keystone service only. No secret material is introduced. strconv.Itoa(int(*pointer)) is used to stringify CRD-validated integers — no injection vector.

architecture_checklist.notes: New KeystoneSpec fields live alongside the existing PriorityClassName/TopologySpreadConstraints pattern. Strategy uses *appsv1.DeploymentStrategy so the upstream type is the source of truth — no leaky wrapper. Graceful-termination logic is concentrated in three pure helpers in reconcile_deployment.go; validation is concentrated in the existing validate() method; webhook does not grow new branches in Default(). Layering (types -> webhook -> reconciler) is respected; webhook never depends on reconciler code.

dry_yagni_checklist.notes: Helpers are flat one-purpose functions; no interface/strategy pattern introduced for what is essentially value lookup with a default. deploymentStrategy constructs the default inline rather than via a global var, so operator intent is clear at the call site. No speculative flags beyond the four documented in the acceptance criteria.

fail_fast_checklist.notes: Webhook rejects every invalid combination at admission time (the loudest possible boundary): below-min values, preStop>=grace, harakiri>=drain-window, keepAliveTimeout without keepAlive, Recreate+rollingUpdate-block. Reconciler uses defense-in-depth defaults rather than panicking on nil, consistent with the operator-upgrade compatibility requirement (REQ-015/REQ-016). Chainsaw E2E catch: blocks dump rich diagnostics (pod logs, events, rollout history) on failure so regressions surface with enough context to triage.

defensive_checklist.notes: uwsgiCommand strictly gates both new optional flags with `uwsgi != nil && uwsgi.Harakiri != nil` and `uwsgi != nil && uwsgi.HTTPKeepAliveTimeout != nil && httpKeepAlive`, eliminating the empty-flag risk. terminationGracePeriodSeconds / preStopSleepSeconds / deploymentStrategy all check the relevant pointer before dereferencing and otherwise return the documented default. Load-gen Job uses ttlSecondsAfterFinished:300 + backoffLimit:0 + activeDeadlineSeconds:180 to guarantee it is reaped; monitor subshell is killed and waited on explicitly in step 3g.

suggested_improvements.suggestion: When terminationGracePeriodSeconds is user-supplied and fails the min>=10 check, the cross-field `preStopSleep >= terminationGracePeriod` branch can also fire against the same user value, yielding two errors for what is logically one configuration mistake. Not incorrect (both messages are accurate) but a future micro-tightening could skip the cross-field check when the range check already rejected the input. Keep as-is unless user feedback complains about duplicated errors.

The test reviewer-comment in 01-patch-image.yaml and chainsaw-test.yaml already flags the curlimages/curl:8.10.1 preload dependency. Worth capturing in the kind provisioning workflow (e.g. a short PR follow-up that adds the image to the preload list). Not a blocker — the test will surface the missing image with ImagePullBackOff + diagnostic dump if it is ever not preloaded.

The `httpKeepAliveTimeout <= preStopSleepSeconds` row is documented as 'Operator policy (not enforced)'. Consider adding a webhook warning (not error) in a follow-up so operators get a soft nudge without breaking existing configurations. Not required for CC-0084 since the current design intentionally keeps this as a recommendation.

next_steps: Merge CC-0084 to main once CI (including the chainsaw e2e lane) is green.
Schedule a follow-up micro-ticket to preload curlimages/curl:8.10.1 in the kind provisioning workflow so the new rolling-update-zero-downtime lane never hits ImagePullBackOff on fresh runners.
Optionally open a follow-up to deduplicate webhook errors when the min-check already rejected a field (see suggestion #1).

detected_patterns.note: Explicitly called out as REQ-007/REQ-003 (CC-0084) in the code. All four new Minimum-marked fields are re-validated in Go in addition to the CRD schema, matching the CC-0011/CC-0040 precedent in the same method.

detected_patterns.pattern: Nil-safe defaulting helpers mirroring CC-0075 priorityClassName pattern
detected_patterns.note: Each helper dereferences the *T spec field if non-nil, otherwise returns the documented default. Fresh value constructed per call (including intstr pointers inside DeploymentStrategy) so results are safe to reuse across reconciles without aliasing.

detected_patterns.pattern: Strict nil-pointer gating for optional flag emission
detected_patterns.note: `if uwsgi != nil && uwsgi.Harakiri != nil` and `if uwsgi != nil && uwsgi.HTTPKeepAliveTimeout != nil && httpKeepAlive` prevents emitting --harakiri or --http-keepalive-timeout with an empty argument. The httpKeepAlive gate in the reconciler matches the webhook rejection rule so the two layers are consistent.

detected_patterns.pattern: Unconditional Spec.Strategy assignment via value-returning helper
detected_patterns.note: `Strategy: deploymentStrategy(keystone)` always writes a concrete DeploymentStrategy — there is no zero-value / missing-field code path. Verified by TestBuildKeystoneDeployment_DefaultRollingUpdateStrategy and TestBuildKeystoneDeployment_StrategyStableAcrossReconciles.

detected_patterns.pattern: CRD manifest sync between helm/ and config/crd/bases/
detected_patterns.note: Bodies are byte-identical; the helm copy carries only the three-line CC-0017 SOURCE/sync-instructions header. `diff <(tail -n +4 helm-crd.yaml) config-crd.yaml` is empty.

detected_patterns.pattern: Chainsaw E2E orchestration with in-cluster load generator + background monitor
detected_patterns.note: Single orchestration script applies a Job, waits for it to start, launches a 1s-cadence availableReplicas poller, triggers the image-tag patch mid-load, waits for Job completion, then persists summaries to /tmp for downstream assertion steps. This isolates orchestration (needs background tasks) from assertion (chainsaw `assert:` friendly).

detected_patterns.pattern: Feature-ID citations in code, tests, CRDs, manifests, and docs
detected_patterns.note: Every new block of logic, test, YAML fixture, and doc section names CC-0084 (often alongside the specific REQ id). Matches repository convention.
